draft.title: Gradient of an interval
card: Gradient measures how steep a line is. Gradient = rise ÷ run, where rise is the change in y and run is the change in x.
For two points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂), the gradient is (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁). Subtract the coordinates in the same order on top and bottom.
A line that slopes up to the right has a positive gradient. A line that slopes down to the right has a negative gradient.
Example: from (1, 7) to (4, 1), rise = 1 − 7 = −6 and run = 4 − 1 = 3. Gradient = −6 ÷ 3 = −2.
draft.remember: Gradient is change in y over change in x, and it is negative when the line goes down to the right.

a.q: What is the gradient of the interval from (2, 3) to (6, 11)?
a.why: Rise = 11 − 3 = 8 and run = 6 − 2 = 4, so the gradient is 8 ÷ 4 = 2. The option 1/2 turns the fraction upside down by putting run over rise.
a.clue: Put the change in y on top.

b.q: A walking track on a map runs from A(1, 9) to B(5, 3). What is its gradient?
b.why: Rise = 3 − 9 = −6 and run = 5 − 1 = 4, so the gradient is −6/4 = −3/2. The track slopes down to the right, so the gradient is negative. The option 3/2 loses the sign.
b.clue: Does the line go up or down as x increases?
